extraFacts.fact: Unit conversions: 1 bar = 14.5038 psi, so 145 psi is about 10 bar and 150 psi about 10.3 bar. Temperature: deg C = (deg F - 32) / 1.8, so -10 deg F is about -23 deg C, +5 deg F about -15 deg C, +115 deg F about 46 deg C, +120 deg F about 49 deg C and +125 deg F about 52 deg C.

A 2-way valve opens or closes one flow path (normally closed means it blocks flow when de-energised); a 3-way valve has 3 ports and 2 positions; a 4-way or 5-port valve has 4 or 5 ports and 2 positions, and a 3-position valve adds a centre position. In the centre position of a 4/3 or 5/3 valve, all ports blocked (closed centre) holds the cylinder, centre exhaust vents both cylinder ports and pressure centre pressurises both. A single-solenoid spring or air return valve goes back when de-energised; a double-solenoid 2-position valve stays in the last position commanded.
extraFacts.source: ISO 1219-1 (fluid power graphical symbols); Indus Hydraulics guide 'Solenoid valve functions explained: 3/2, 5/2 and 5/3 valves'

extraFacts.fact: A solenoid coil is built for one supply type and voltage (for example 24 V DC or 120 V AC); a coil on the wrong voltage or supply type will not switch the valve and can burn out. An internal-pilot valve takes its pilot air from the main supply; an external-pilot valve needs a separate pilot supply, used when the main pressure is low or the valve runs on vacuum.
extraFacts.source: ISO 4414 (pneumatic fluid power, general rules and safety requirements); Parker Pneumatic Division valve catalogues

extraFacts.fact: ISO 5599-2 and ISO 15407-2 are mounting-interface standards for five-port pneumatic directional valves: they fix the mounting-surface dimensions and port layout so that valves built to the same interface size can be changed on one sub-base or manifold.
extraFacts.source: ISO 5599-2 and ISO 15407-2, pneumatic fluid power five-port directional control valves, mounting interface surfaces

extraFacts.fact: NEMA 4 is an enclosure type for indoor or outdoor use that gives protection against windblown dust, rain, splashing water and hose-directed water; it is not an explosion-proof or hazardous-area rating.
extraFacts.source: NEMA 250, Enclosures for Electrical Equipment (1000 Volts Maximum)

extraFacts.fact: Cv is a flow coefficient: the higher the Cv, the more air a valve passes at a given pressure drop; the Cv of the valve should be compared with the Cv the cylinder circuit needs. A valve manifold or sub-base carries several valves on one supply and exhaust passage.
extraFacts.source: ANSI/ISA-75.01.01 flow coefficient definition; Indus Hydraulics guide 'Sizing pneumatic valves: Cv, Kv, sonic conductance'
